objective: REMEDIATION (v2): Off-grid buildings produce water and sewage from nothing. The WaterWell struct exists (society/housing.rs:101-128) but is never constructed, never linked to the regional WaterReserveState (utilities/hydro_grid.rs), and its yield is a static scalar that bypasses draw_groundwater. Sewage generation is a fixed per-occupant table (utilities/demand.rs:63-219) that is never gated by actual water extracted. Off-grid waste/sewage does not route to LocalPollutionState (environment/smog.rs). Fix all four defects with concrete physical mechanics: water must be physically extracted from the aquifer before consumption; sewage volume must equal MIN(water_extracted, consumption_demand); off-grid sewage must convert to standalone_biohazard mass in LocalPollutionState; CAPEX BOM must use Steel/Concrete (not Stone/Timber/Bricks). v2 CORRECTIONS: (1) Aquifer recharge is FRACTIONAL based on regional precipitation, NOT a full reset to capacity each turn â€” wells CAN deplete. (2) Pre-existing world-generation off-grid buildings spawn with constructed = true wells to avoid a Day-1 steel/concrete demand shock; construction logic is strictly for NEW developments built after world generation.

physical_mechanics.aquifer_link: Add aquifer_capacity_liters and aquifer_quality fields to Region in society/geography.rs (surgical append, Rule 23). These are physical geological properties set during world generation. aquifer_capacity_liters is the hard upper bound on groundwater_volume (Rule 20: physical boundaries). aquifer_quality (0.0-1.0) scales well yield and water quality.
physical_mechanics.well_construction: Add a construction routing path so NEW off-grid HousingBuildings (built after world generation) can build a WaterWell. When a building's active_water_supply is a standalone method (Local Well, Hand Pump Well, etc.) and water_well is None, the owner (company or cooperative) must issue a B2B construction order: CAPEX BOM = Steel + Concrete + machinery (NOT Stone/Timber/Bricks). BOM quantities scale by well_depth_m and building_capacity (Rule 15: physical scaling). Construction progresses per turn until construction_progress >= 1.0, then constructed = true. Until constructed, standalone_water_yield = 0.0 (no water from thin air). CRITICAL v2 CORRECTION: Pre-existing world-generation off-grid buildings MUST spawn with a fully constructed well (constructed = true, construction_progress = 1.0) at world generation time. This avoids a Day-1 economy crash where every off-grid building simultaneously issues B2B steel/concrete orders that exceed available supply. The generator (engine/generator/corporate.rs) must initialize water_well = Some(WaterWell { constructed: true, construction_progress: 1.0, depth_m: <regional groundwater depth>, max_yield_liters: <computed>, ... }) for off-grid buildings at world generation. Construction logic (B2B orders, progress per turn) is strictly for NEW developments built after Turn 0.
physical_mechanics.well_extraction_from_aquifer: Replace standalone_water_yield (housing.rs:768-778) with a function that calls region.water_reserves.draw_groundwater(well_demand). The well demands min(max_yield_liters, consumption_demand) liters. draw_groundwater (hydro_grid.rs:194-198) hard-clamps to available groundwater_volume and decrements it. Returns (drawn_liters, water_quality). The drawn volume is the ACTUAL water_extracted â€” not a static scalar. v2 CORRECTION â€” FRACTIONAL RECHARGE: groundwater_volume does NOT reset to aquifer_capacity each turn. Instead, WaterReserveState::regenerate must add a FRACTIONAL recharge volume based on regional precipitation: recharge_volume = precipitation_mm * recharge_coefficient * aquifer_recharge_area. This is a small per-turn increment, NOT a full reset. Wells CAN deplete the aquifer if extraction exceeds recharge (drought / over-pumping scenario). When groundwater_volume == 0, well yields 0.0 (aquifer depleted â€” Rule 20). The aquifer slowly recovers over many turns via fractional recharge. This makes the abandonment mechanic meaningful: a depleted well must be abandoned and the building must either wait for recharge, build a deeper well, or connect to municipal water.
physical_mechanics.sewage_gating: In utilities/consumption.rs, after computing water_consumed (lines 107-126), derive sewage_volume = water_consumed.min(demand.sewage_generation). A building with zero water_extracted produces zero sewage. A building with partial water produces partial sewage. Sewage is bounded by BOTH extracted water AND occupancy-based demand. This enforces mass conservation: sewage mass <= water mass extracted from aquifer.
physical_mechanics.off_grid_pollution_routing: Add off_grid_waste_emission function in environment/smog.rs. Accepts (sewage_volume_liters, solid_waste_mass, building_id, region_id). Converts sewage_volume to standalone_biohazard_mass via a physical conversion factor (liters â†’ biohazard mass, e.g., 0.001 kg/liter for raw sewage). Converts solid_waste to waste_dumping_biohazard via existing waste_grid.rs logic. Writes to LocalPollutionState.standalone_biohazard and LocalPollutionState.waste_dumping_biohazard. Wire this function from process_utility_consumption in consumption.rs for every off-grid building. Municipal/sewer-connected buildings route to sewer_network instead (existing path).
physical_mechanics.capex_bom_fix: Replace WaterWell::compute_capex_bom (housing.rs:158-182) to use Steel (casing/lining), Concrete (shaft seal), and machinery (pump head, if powered). Quantities scale by well_depth_m and building_capacity. Remove Stone/Timber/Bricks. Steel and Concrete are existing commodities procured via B2B from existing warehouses (architectural parsimony â€” Rule 14).
